 Judgment

The petitioner has filed the present claim petition against the respondents under section 166 of MV Act seeking compensation towards the accidental injuries from date of accident till the date of payment together with cost and interest.

2. The factual matrix of the petition in the nutshell is as follows:
On 30.06.2023 at about 00.30 to 00.32 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding in motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-45-L-7801 at 1st cross, 1st main road, JP Nagar, 7th Stage,
A r a k e r e M i c o l a y o u t , B e n g a l u r u . A t t h a t t i m e o n e c a r b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-05-NH-3354 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner vehicle from opposite direction.
Due to the impact of accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to various parts of the body.
3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Fortis Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as an in inpatient.
X-ray report reveals that petitioner sustained right tibia condyle fracture and he was discharged with an advice for continuing follow up treatment with complete bed rest.

4. The petitioner further pleaded that he has incurred Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
conveyance, medical treatment, attendant, nursing care and other incidental expenses.
He is in need of future medical treatment and other incidental expenses.
5. Petitioner further submits that, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 31 years as on the date of accident.

He was working as Delivery boy at Zomato Company and was earning Rs.20,600/-
per month.
He was maintaining his family out of said source of income and was a sole bread earner to his family.
Due to the accidental injuries he could not able to do any kind of work compared to his previous strategy.
The disability sustained in the accident has impacted on his earning capacity and as such himself and his family have suffered a lot by mentally, physically and financially.
6. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driver of the respondent No.2, who drive his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NG-3354.

The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said vehicle thereby the vicarious liability is operated on respondent No.1 on the indemnified contract and as such, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
7. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till realization.
8. After registration of the petition, notices were issued against respondents.
Inspite of service of the notice, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before this court.
Hence, after due service of notice against the respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 is placed exparte.

In pursuance of service of Shashikumar K C vs Edelweiss General Insurance Co., Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14812159/
2 notice the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsels and filed their written statement on behalf of respondent No.1 by denying the entire petition averments.

conveyance and nourishment of the said petitioner.

prays to dismiss the petition.

In addition to his evidence, the petitioner got examined doctor,
who has issued disability certificate for the injuries sustained by the petitioner as PW.2.

10. Heard the arguments on both side and perused the materials on record.

11. Based on the above said pleading, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NG-3354 by its driver, in RTA took place on 30.06.2023 at about 00.30 a.m., on 1st Cross and 1st Main Road,
Arakere Mico Layout, JP Nagar, 7th Phase, Ben- galuru City?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
12. My findings on the above issues are as under.

 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative,

3 13. The petitioner has made stand towards fact and factum of the accident that on 30.06.2023 at about 00.30 to 00.32 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding in motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-45-L-7801 at 1 st cross, 1st main road, JP Nagar, 7th Stage, Arakere Micolayout,
Bengaluru.
At that time one car bearing Reg.No.KA-05- NH-3354 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner vehicle from opposite direction.
Due to the impact of accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to various parts of the body.

14. The petitioner has claimed compensation against the respondents urging that the alleged accident took place on the alleged date, time, place and thereby the petitioner was called upon to substantiate the said stand.
15. By responding to the one way burden the petitioner has come up with oral and documentary evidence.
The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents in total on his behalf.
Further, PW.1 has got marked 11 documents on his behalf as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.

Further,
the petitioner got examined doctor as PW.2, who has issued disability certificate to him and got marked 2 documents through the said PW.2 as per Ex.P12 and Ex.P13.
Further, the petitioner got examined the Medical Record Officer, Forties Hospital, as PW.3 has got marked 2 documents as per Ex.P14 and Ex.P.15.
In his chief-examination, PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments and has specifically stated that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offender vehicle.
16. The petitioner was subjected to cross- examination by learned counsel for respondent No.1.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.
17. The Respondent No.1 has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1.
RW.1 has reiterated the contents of written statement filed by the respondent No.1 in his examination in chief.

RW.1 was subjected to cross-examination by learned counsel for petitioner during the course of cross-examination of petitioner he had admitted that he has deposed his evidence on the basis of documents submitted by him.
He does not have any personal knowledge about the case.
The policy was in force as on the date of occurrence of the accident.
The police have filed charge sheet against the driver of our insured vehicle.
18. The accident in question is not in dispute.

Whereas Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint,
Ex.P.3 and 4 are the spot mahazar along with sketch, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report, Ex.P9 is the charge sheet which clearly shows that, on the alleged date, time and place of the accident has occurred and in the said accident the offender vehicle is involved in the occurrence of the same.
19. The above referred documents clearly indicates that, the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.2 offender vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NG-3354.
It is clear from the records that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and extended with treatment.
There is no any adverse material available to disbelieve the stand taken by the petitioner to the extent of the factum of accident as introduced by him.
Thus, this tribunal has answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: The petitioner has claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till its realization.
On the basis of the materials on record, it is necessary to examine claim of petitioner in appropriate manner.
In support of the case petitioner has come up with various materials.
As such it is necessary to examined the materials on record in the parameter of pecuniary and non-pecuniary character.

1. Pecuniary loss:- This head of compensation includes compensation towards the loss of earning capacity, medical and future medical expenditure, expenditure incurred towards conveyance allowance, attendant charges, special diet and other miscellaneous expenditure.
As such these aspects are to be examined by examining the available materials on record.
(A) Loss of earning capacity and loss of future income/earnings:-

In order to determine the compensation under this head, it is necessary to consider the age of injured person, occupation, quantum of income, nature of injuries,
percentage of disability and multiplier applicable are to be worked out on the available materials.
( i) The age and applicable multiplier:- The petitioner has contended in his petition that, as on the date of accident he was aged about 31 years.

The material pertaining to Cr.No.247/23 and other medical documents contemplated as on the date of accident,
the petitioner was aged about 31 years.
In addition to that, the petitioner has placed his reliance on the copy of aadhar card.
The said aadhar card reflected the date of birth of petitioner as 07.08.1992.
The accident has occurred on 30.06.2023.

Upon computing the age of the petitioner based on all these materials, it clearly shows that,
the petitioner is aged of 31 years as on the date of occurrence of accident.
As per the documentary evidence available on record, the age of the petitioner is considered as 31 years as on the date of the accident.

Applying the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others Case reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298,
the multiplier of 16 is applicable to the present content.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others Case reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the multiplier of 16 is considered to determine the claim made herein.

(ii) The occupation of petitioner and quantum of income:- The petitioner has contended that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and was Delivery boy, Zomato Company and he was earning Rs.20,600/- per month.
He has not produced any documents to prove the said income.
Hence, in the absence of express proof, it is necessary to determine the income of the petitioner based on the principles of notional income.
The Karnataka State Legal Service Authority has fixed a chart for notional income.
By placing reliance on the said income slab.
The income of the petitioner is to be determined.

As per the said chart the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month as operated to the year Shashikumar K C vs Edelweiss General Insurance Co., Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14812159/
5 2023.

(iii) Nature of injury and percentage of disability:-

To prove the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner he has examined one doctor Chidanand K.J.C., Orthopedic Surgeon and Lecturer Orthopedics, Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics, Bengaluru, is examined as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.P.12 and Ex.P.13.

sentences.text: PW.2/doctor has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained right tibial condyl fracture.
This witness has opined that, petitioner has sustained total disability of lower limb at 35% and permanent physical disability to the whole body at 11.66%.
The injuries are permanent in nature.
Petitioner has contended that, he is a Delivery boy and assessed disability causes effect on the avocation of petitioner.
Hence, the disability is considered at 11.66%.
The said extent of disability is considerable to determine the compensation under this head.

To prove the nature of his injuries the petitioner has examined one Raghu.Y.C. MRO at Forties Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW.3, though him, authorization letter and ER record of petitioner by name Shashikumar K.C. along with Medico legal form are marked under Ex.P.14 and 15.
These documents shows that petitioner has taken treatment in Forties Hospital, Bengaluru.
Annual income X Multiplier X permanent physical disability = Loss of earning capacity.
Thereby the petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,58,195/- towards loss of earning capacity and future earnings.
The petitioner being a Delivery boy and contended that, he used to earn Rs.20,600/- per month.
As the petitioner has not produced any documents to prove his income.
In the absence of proof, the notional income is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Under the circumstances, the per day income of the petitioner would arrive at Rs.534/-.
(B) Medical expenditure:-

The petitioner contended that, he has incurred Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance,
medical treatment, attendant and nursing care expenses.
The petitioner has not produced the medical bills and also discharge summary.
Hence, he is not entitled for the same.

(C) Future medical expenditure, Conveyance allowances, attendant charge and special diet and Loss of income during the laid up period:-
The petitioner has not claimed compensation towards future medical expenditure for follow up treatment but, the petitioner has not produced the medical bills and also discharge summary to show that he has spent amount for even for conveyance allowances, attendant charge and special diet.
Hence, he is not entitled for compensation under this head.
21. Non-Pecuniary Loss:-
This element of compensation reads as follows;

6 (a) Pain and sufferings and mental agony:-

entities.text: K C vs Edelweiss General Insurance Co., Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to medical records, the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries at the age of 31 years as on the date of accident.
The said accidental injuries have caused him lot of pain to suffer in his future life span.

In The Civil Appeal No. 8510 Of 2022 Sidram V/S The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. And Anr, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "Pain and suffering would be categorized as a non-pecuniary loss as it is incapable of being arithmetically calculated.

entities.text: Sidram V/S The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, when compensation is to be awarded for pain and suffering, special circumstances of the claimant have to be taken into account including the victim's age, the unusual deprivation the victim has suffered, the effect thereof on his or her future life."

Like wise, in the case of Subulaxmi V/s Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation and another (2012) 10 SCC 177 the Hon'ble Supreme Court awarded compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.

entities.text: Subulaxmi V/s Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation and another (2012) 10 SCC 177
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the above formula to the case on hand and by considering the nature of the injuries and percentage of disability caused to the petitioner, the petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

(b) Loss of enjoyment of life and amenities of life:-
The available on records reveals that the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries at the age of 31 years as on the date of accident.
In R.D. Hattangadi V/s M/s Pest Control (India) Private Ltd., (1995) 1 SCC 551

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi V/s M/s Pest Control (India) Private Ltd., (1995) 1 SCC 551
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the Hon'ble Supreme Court while dealing with the different heads of compensation in injury cases has held that "this includes a variety of matters such as the inability to walk, run or sit, etc.
We include here too the loss of childhood pleasure such as the ability to freely play, dance, run, etc., the loss of ability to freely move or travel without assistance.
Then, there is the virtual impossibility of marriage as well as a complete loss of the ability to have sex and to have and nurture children."
Applying the same formula to the case on hand this shows that the injuries caused to petitioner has impacted on the enjoyment of his personal life and amenities of life.
Hence, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.60,000/- under this head.

23.
Admittedly, the respondent No.1 and 2 are the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer is bound to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Hence, respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
24.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,18,195/- {future medical expenses shall not carry any interest}, with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
